Theme

Nature & food

agricultural adjective

also agriculture, farming (adj.), rural, of the farm

classical

Cic. de Or. 1.69: rēs rūstica (Lewis & Short)
Cato Agr. 5.4: opus rūsticum omne

rūsticus, rūstica, rūsticum

agricultural, of farming and the country

Of the country as against the town (the opposite of urbānus), and so of farming: rēs rūstica is agriculture, the subject of Varro’s Rērum rūsticārum librī and Columella’s Dē rē rūsticā. Of a person it can also mean boorish, unpolished.

Other words

  • agrī cultūra, agrī cultūrae f. — agriculture, farming

    also used · classical · Cic. Sen. 54 (Lewis & Short)

    Also written as one word, agricultūra; Cato’s book is Dē agrī cultūrā.

  • agrārius, agrāria, agrārium — of land; of the distribution of public land

    also used · classical · Liv. 2.41: lēx agrāria (Lewis & Short)

    Classically a legal and political word, of land laws (lēgēs agrāriae), not of farming in general.

Examples

  • nam rēs rūstica sīc est, sī ūnam rem sērō fēceris, omnia opera sērō faciēs

    for farming is like this: if you do one thing late, you’ll do every job lateCato Agr. 5.7

  • rūsticus Rōmānus factus es

    you’ve become a Roman countrymanCic. Fam. 16.21.7

See also farm, farmer, countryside, livestock.
